newsitem.title: USA: U.S. unemployment unchanged at 5.2 percent in October.
newsitem.headline: U.S. unemployment unchanged at 5.2 percent in October.

text.p: The unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent in October, the Labour Department said Friday, as the economy resumed producing new jobs at a healthy pace.
In the government's first look at the the economy's vitality last month, the department said the number of non-farm jobs rose by 210,000 after falling a revised 35,000 in September.
Wall Steet economists surveyed by Reuters had projected the unemployment rate steady at 5.2 percent and the creation of 212,000 jobs.

The new data comes just two days after the government reported that the economy braked hard in the third quarter, showing a growth rate of only 2.2 percent after speeding ahead at 4.7 percent rate in the second quarter.
Average hourly earnings of workers, which have come under the microscope of late as an indicator of inflation, also were unchanged after being up a revised four cents in September.

"It's a perfect number," said Evelina Tainer, chief economist at Indosuez Carr Futures. "The Fed's going to love it. It puts the three-month average at 152,000, which means we're growing at a nice pace but not too slow, not too fast."

The inflation-sensitive U.S. Treasury market jumped as investors bought heavily after the employment report. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond gained more than 3/4 of a point and its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, dropped to a new seven-month low of 6.59 percent from 6.64 percent Thursday.

The report will be added to the Federal Reserve's deliberations when it meets Nov. 13 to decide the future course of interest rates. Strong job growth will send out some alarms, although the lack of wage inflation should be good news.
The department said services industries added 119,000 jobs, the largest gain since May, as amusement and recreation added jobs while industry in general showed relatively light layoffs.
Following little growth in August and September, the retail trade added 62,000 jobs in October, with gains fairly widespread.
Government employment continued to show decreases in October, falling an additional 40,000, while employment in both finance and real estate rose sharply.
Manufacturing employment rose 6,000 after falling in September.
